the extreme abundance of lingual valves in some outcropping sequences of the Paranà Basin, and the absence of lingulids in others, are the result of a complex interplay of intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

lingulid-rich sequences are a taphofacies, that they are found in a variety of settings (from the lower shoreface to the shallow offshore) and that their occurrence is controlled by intrinsic factors (e.g., shell thickness) and extrinsic factors (e.g, storms).

lingulids were the dominant brachiopods in Devonian shallow marine environments of the Paraná basin, and that the occurrence of lingulids is a useful tool in palaeoenvironmental reconstructions of these environments, as they represent a taphofacies that can be recognized in sedimentary sequences.

the analysis of a fossil accumulation that represents a taphonomic window into the ecology and behaviour of lingulids.
the taphonomic and sedimentological controls on the occurrence of lingulids in the Devonian sequences, and the recognition of the taphofacies that they represent.
the taphonomic and taphofacial aspects of lingulid-rich outcrops of Devonian sequences in the Parana Basin.

lingulid tafonomy is controlled mainly by intrinsic features of the lingulids, such as shell thickness, and by the extrinsic factors of sedimentation and burial rate, which are in turn controlled by the energy regime of the depositional environment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
lingulid-rich sequences can be used as a proxy for the reconstruction of the paleoenvironmental setting of the Devonian of the Parana basin.
the Devonian lingulid-rich outcrops are not the product of a single taphonomic process.
